input_summary.task_description_excerpt: 本任务旨在基于 MatBench ExptGAP 数据集构建监督回归模型，用于预测无机材料的实验带隙（Band gap, eV）。模型以材料的化学组成信息为输入，通过组成特征提取、数据清洗、特征标准化以及候选回归模型训练，学习材料组成与带隙之间的映射关系。任务重点包括合理构建材料描述符、选择适合小规模材料数据的机器学习模型、采用交叉验证评估模型泛化性能，并使用 MAE、RMSE 和 R² 等指标衡量预测精度，最终获得可用于实验带隙快速预测与材料筛选的机器学习模型。
input_summary.dataset_description_excerpt: matbench_expt_gap 是材料科学机器学习基准 MatBench 中的回归任务数据集，包含约 4600 个无机材料样本。它仅以化学成分为输入，目标为实验测得的带隙值（单位 eV），无晶体结构信息，数据经标准化清洗，专门用于评估模型仅通过成分预测材料实验带隙的能力。
constraints: ai所做的决策要依据数据情况和材料科学知识综合分析，并给出决策的理由.

workflow_rationale.overall_reasoning_summary: This workflow is designed to predict experimental band gap (eV) from composition alone by extracting a wide range of physically motivated features (elemental statistics, stoichiometry, oxidation states, ionicity, band center, valence orbitals). Feature selection and scaling will handle the resulting dimensionality. A suite of regression models—linear with regularization and tree‑based ensembles—will be compared using 5‑fold cross‑validation, with MAE as the primary metric. Interpretability will be assessed via SHAP and permutation importance to connect features with band gap physics. The target will be log‑transformed to mitigate skewness. The baseline ridge model ensures a minimum performance reference.
key_assumptions: Composition is the primary determinant of band gap; structural and processing effects are secondary.
The dataset has been curated and contains no hidden errors beyond the reported skewness and outliers.
All chemical formulas can be parsed by pymatgen; invalid formulas will be excluded.
Log‑transformation of the target will improve model stability and reduce heteroscedasticity.
known_risks: Some formulas may fail to parse, leading to data loss.
High feature dimensionality (~200 features) could cause overfitting, especially for linear models without proper regularization.
Experimental band gap values may contain measurement uncertainties that limit achievable prediction accuracy.
Log transformation may not fully normalize the target distribution.
planning_warnings: Target variable is highly skewed (skewness = 1.93) and contains outliers; robust scaling/metrics and target transformation are strongly advised.
Interpretability of complex ensemble models will rely on post‑hoc methods (SHAP), which can be computationally intensive.
Feature engineering will produce many correlated features; feature selection or L1 regularization is essential to avoid overfitting.
Composition‑only input may miss structural contributions that influence band gap, limiting the best possible performance.
planning_assumptions: The dataset is representative of the inorganic crystal space and has no systematic biases.
Log1p transformation is suitable; if it degrades performance, the workflow can revert to using robust models on the original scale.
Featurizers will handle all provided formulas; if not, fallback to basic composition features is acceptable.
Cross‑validation splits are random and no sample leakage occurs.
workflow_rationale.llm_reasoning_summary: Based on the task specification and data profile, a composition‑only featurization strategy using elemental statistics (Magpie), stoichiometry, oxidation states, ionic properties, band center, and valence orbitals is optimal. Regularized linear models (ridge, lasso) provide interpretability and robustness, while tree ensembles (random forest, gradient boosting) maximize accuracy. K‑fold CV and MAE as the primary metric ensure reliable evaluation. Target transformation and feature selection address skewness and dimensionality. The plan balances user priorities of accuracy, interpretability, and robustness, with explicit fallback options for risks.

items.allocation_rationale: Baseline model — fixed defaults, no HPO needed.

Lasso has a small search space (primarily alpha). 4 trials are sufficient to explore a range of regularization strengths given the modest feature count (24) and large sample size (4604). More trials would yield diminishing returns.

Random forest has moderate complexity (n_estimators, max_depth, min_samples_split). With 4604 samples, 6 trials allow exploration of key parameters without excessive computational cost. It is less sensitive to hyperparameters than boosting.

Gradient boosting (sklearn) has moderate sensitivity to learning_rate, n_estimators, and max_depth. 6 trials provide a fair search given that it shares the boosting concept with xgboost but is often slower to converge.

XGBoost is the most promising model for low MAE on this dataset, but it has the largest and most sensitive hyperparameter set (n_estimators, learning_rate, max_depth, subsample, colsample_bytree, regularization). 8 trials are allocated to thoroughly explore its search space within the 30-trial budget.

SVR with RBF kernel requires tuning of C and gamma, but training time per trial is higher due to quadratic complexity. 6 trials balance the need to find good parameters with the risk of excessive runtime. Its expected performance is lower than boosting, so it receives fewer trials than xgboost.
